l7hu-stakes:
Heads-Up is poker's purest form. Compared with 6-max or full ring, HU has these characteristics:

1. Bigger positional value: the BTN has positional advantage every hand
2. Much wider ranges: any pair is strong, any Ax is strong
3. More frequent postflop decisions: more often only two players contest the pot
4. More important exploitative adjustments: you can quickly identify and exploit opponent weaknesses
Core concept: positional value is huge in HU. The BTN has positional advantage every hand. Any pair is strong in HU, and any Ax is strong.
Preflop and Postflop: Two Widening Lines

HU preflop ranges are much wider than 6-max:

BTN/SB open range: about 80% (far above the widest 6-max BTN opening tier)
- Any pair is strong
- Any Ax is strong
- Suited connectors and small pairs can all open

3-bet range:
- Wider (about 10-15%)
- Includes strong hands + some bluffs
- Balance matters more

The key HU postflop adjustments:

1. More C-Bets: the BTN has range advantage and should C-Bet at high frequency
2. Wider value bets: top pair weak kicker is also a strong hand
3. More bluffs: the opponent's range is wider, easier to bluff off
4. Positional use: with position you can value-bet and bluff more frequently

Postflop stack budget is measured with SPR (SPR = effective stack ÷ flop pot):

HU 100BB: the SB min-raises to 2BB and the BB calls → flop pot 4BB with 98BB behind:
SPR = 98 ÷ 4 = 24.5 (deep stack: all three streets playable, top pair wants pot control)

The same hand in a 3-bet pot: the SB opens 2BB, the BB raises to 9BB, the SB calls → flop pot 18.5BB with 80BB behind:
SPR = 80 ÷ 18.5 ≈ 4.3 (low SPR: top pair good kicker is committed in two streets)

How to read it: HU ranges are wide and opponents pay off wide, so the same top pair only takes two or three small bets at SPR 24.5 but puts the stack in at SPR 4.3 — HU "wider value betting" is set by SPR and range width together, not by "betting harder".

Theory support: reading position, ranges and frequencies as one map instead of four isolated rules is Theory Academy T9 "Full Integration" — that chapter folds HU opening width, postflop frequency and sizing into a single decision tree, and this lesson's four HU differences are its entry layer.
Adapting to Different HU Opponent Types

Quickly identify HU opponent types and adjust:

1. Tight-passive: C-Bet frequently, bluff more
2. Loose-passive: value-bet more, bluff less
3. Loose-aggressive: balanced play, some traps
4. Tight-aggressive: respect the opponent, avoid excessive conflict
The most important HU skill is quickly identifying the opponent type and adjusting. Build a basic portrait in the first 20 hands, then start exploiting.
Warning: don't play HU with 6-max standards. Many hands that are folds in 6-max are calls or raises in HU.

Theory support: why you must both hold the baseline and deviate by opponent type is Theory Academy T9 "GTO-Exploitation Unified Framework" — the baseline keeps you unexploited when information is thin, deviations earn extra expectation when information is rich, and this lesson's four opponent portraits are its execution entry.

HU basics in three lines:
Open about 80% of hands, then set value bets by range width rather than absolute hand strength
The same top pair only bets small for pot control at SPR 24.5, and puts the stack in at SPR 4.3
Opponent type sets the deviation direction: tight-passive → bluff more, loose-passive → value more, loose-aggressive → balance with traps, tight-aggressive → avoid excess conflict

l7hu-stakes-q1.question: The HU BTN/SB open range is about:
l7hu-stakes-q1.explanation: The HU BTN/SB open range is about 80%, far wider than the widest 6-max BTN opening tier (about 35%).

l7hu-stakes-q2.question: Which hand type rises most in value in HU?
l7hu-stakes-q2.explanation: In HU any pair is strong and any Ax is strong — these hands rise sharply in value.

l7hu-stakes-q3.question: Against a tight-passive opponent in HU you should:
l7hu-stakes-q3.explanation: Against a tight-passive opponent C-Bet frequently and bluff more because their fold rate is high.

l7hu-stakes-q4.question: How is positional value in HU?
options: Huge — the BTN has positional advantage every hand
l7hu-stakes-q4.explanation: HU positional value is huge — the BTN has positional advantage every hand.

l7hu-stakes-q5.question: The correct play for top pair weak kicker in HU is:
l7hu-stakes-q5.explanation: HU ranges are wider, so top pair weak kicker is also a strong hand — value bet more widely.

l7hu-stakes-q6.question: HU 100BB: the SB min-raises to 2BB, the BB calls; the flop pot is 4BB and both players have 98BB behind. The SPR here is about:
l7hu-stakes-q6.explanation: SPR = effective stack ÷ flop pot = 98 ÷ 4 = 24.5. About 4.3 is the 3-bet-pot figure (80 ÷ 18.5); about 12 comes from 100 ÷ 8, double-counting both preflop investments into the pot; about 98 is just the effective stack with no division by the pot.

l7hu-stakes-q7.question: The flop pot is 4BB and you bet 2BB (half pot); the opponent folds 40% and you have 70% equity when called. The EV of this thin value bet is about:
l7hu-stakes-q7.explanation: EV = f×P + (1−f)×[e×(P+b) − (1−e)×b] = 0.4×4 + 0.6×(0.7×6 − 0.3×2) = 1.60 + 0.6×3.60 = +3.76BB. +1.60 only counts the fold branch; +2.16 only counts the called branch; +0.60 writes the net gain as (e−f)×b.

l7hu-stakes-q8.question: The player facing the 3-bet flops KQ (top pair good kicker) on K-8-3 with an 18.5BB pot and 80BB behind. At SPR ≈ 4.3 the correct approach is:
options: Plan to get the stack in over two or three streets, starting with about 45% pot on the flop
Check the flop and decide on the river
Continue only if the turn improves
Shove the flop to end the hand
l7hu-stakes-q8.explanation: SPR = 80 ÷ 18.5 ≈ 4.3, so top pair good kicker gets the stack in over two or three streets (about 8BB → about 20BB → all-in); about 45% pot on the flop builds it most naturally. A flop shove folds out bluffs and weak Kx; checking to the river gives away three streets of value; continuing only when improved hands the low-SPR commitment edge back to the opponent.

l7hu-stakes-q9.question: In heads-up, the SB (button) positional edge comes from:
options: Acting last preflop, speaking last on every street
Acting last postflop, gaining one extra piece of information per street
l7hu-stakes-q9.explanation: The SB is the button, and preflop the SB opens while the BB closes the preflop action — the positional edge only shows up postflop, where the SB acts last (IP) with one extra piece of information per street, watching the opponent act before deciding to value bet, control the pot or bluff; closing the preflop action is the BB's right, and mixing the two up assigns the edge to the wrong street.

l7hu-stakes-q10.question: The same A2s is a fold from UTG in 6-max but a standard open from the SB in heads-up. The difference comes from:
options: Facing one opponent, any Ax being strong, and having position postflop
l7hu-stakes-q10.explanation: The boundary is "number of opponents + position": from UTG in 6-max five players behind can still hold strong hands, so the A-high and kicker risk of A2s gets amplified; heads-up faces one player, any Ax is strong, and the SB has postflop position. This transfer only holds in heads-up — the same A2s stays marginal in a multiway pot, so the HU 80% opening width must not be carried back to full ring.

l7hu-stakes-ex1.title: Wide HU BTN Open
reasoning: 76s plays well in HU — open it
The BTN has positional advantage to use postflop
Suited connectors have excellent postflop potential
In HU this is far more valuable relative to 6-max
l7hu-stakes-ex1.mistakeReasoning: Playing HU with 6-max standards misses many profitable opportunities. 76s is a standard HU open.

l7hu-stakes-ex2.title: Thin value postflop: middle pair bets in HU too
reasoning: On the dry 9-5-2 board the BB's defending range rarely holds anything better than middle pair outside 9x
In HU the BB's range is stretched by an 80% opening width, so middle pair equals top pair in 6-max and must bet
A 1/3-pot bet keeps A-high, backdoor draws and unpaired small pairs paying, while keeping room to fold to a check-raise
l7hu-stakes-ex2.mistakeReasoning: That is a 6-max hand-strength chart: middle pair already sits at the top of value in a wide-range game, and checking lets the BB's weak range see the turn for free.

l7hu-stakes-ex3.title: Out of position in a 3-bet pot: top pair commits at low SPR
reasoning: On a Q-high board the BB's 3-bet range is dense with AA, KK, QQ and AQ, so the range advantage sits with the BB
Pot 14BB with 93BB behind gives SPR ≈ 6.6: top pair good kicker can get the stack in over two or three streets
The BB acts first postflop, so a 1/3-pot bet keeps the whole range betting at high frequency and the turn and river keep pushing
l7hu-stakes-ex3.mistakeReasoning: No position does not mean no betting: handing over the betting lead gives the range advantage back when an A or K arrives and throws away three streets of top-pair value.
